samples.summary: Split-divider drag is off by half the divider width, and the comment justifying the new math is backwards
samples.evidence: `const track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth` then `ratio = (ev.clientX - rect.left) / track`. Flexbox resolves the editor pane to `ratio * track` exactly (basis `x%*W` shrinks by `25 * x`, giving `x*(W-25)`), so the editor's width equals `clientX - rect.left` and the divider's LEFT EDGE — not its painted 1px hairline, which sits at `+12.5px` (`padding: 0 12px`, `background-clip: content-box`) — tracks the pointer. The hairline therefore trails the cursor by a constant 12.5px. The added comment claims the old `/rect.width` form "would leave the divider trailing the pointer by up to its own width"; in fact the old form was exact at the midpoint (`p(1-d/W) + d/2 == p` when `p == W/2`) and its error was `d*(p/W - 0.5)`, i.e. at most ±12.5px at the clamp limits — so the change made the mid-drag case worse, not better, and now grows the error uniformly with the widened 25px band. The correct form is `(ev.clientX - rect.left - divider.offsetWidth / 2) / track`. Separately, the grab offset within the 25px band is never captured, so grabbing the band's right edge snaps the hairline up to 12px on pointerdown.

samples.summary: `readOnlyNoteStore`'s `get` trap returns a silent `noop` for every function it does not recognise, including inherited `Object.prototype` methods — so coercing a read-only store handle to a primitive throws, and a future reader fails silently rather than "loudly"
samples.evidence: The final `else` branch assigns `view = noop` for any function-valued property not in `NOTE_STORE_READERS`/`HISTORY_METHODS`/`batch`. `Reflect.get(target, 'toString')` resolves to `Object.prototype.toString` (a function), so `store.toString` and `store.valueOf` both become `noop` returning `undefined`; combined with `getPrototypeOf: () => null` there is no fallback, so `String(store)`, a template literal, or any implicit ToPrimitive on a read-only handle throws `TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value`. `store.constructor` likewise resolves to `noop`, and `store instanceof YorkieNoteStore` is `false`. This also contradicts the file's own stated guarantee (lines 10-13) that "the cost of forgetting to add a genuine reader is `undefined` at its call site: loud, local": because every `NoteStore` member is a method, a reader added tomorrow returns a `noop` whose call yields `undefined` with no error at all — e.g. a hypothetical `getWordCount()` would silently produce `undefined`/`NaN` downstream on every viewer mount. Nothing on the paths in this diff coerces a store, so the reach is contained today.

samples.summary: `expiresIn` is defaulted with `??`, so an empty-string env value survives and makes every service-token signing throw inside the injector
samples.evidence: `expiresIn: string = process.env.YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN ?? '10m'` and, in `yorkie.service.ts:52-54`, `this.configService.get<string>('YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN') ?? '10m'`. `??` only substitutes for `null`/`undefined`, so a `.env` line `YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN=` yields `''`, which is then cast unchecked to `ms.StringValue` and handed to `jsonwebtoken`, which throws `"expiresIn" should be a number of seconds or string representing a timespan`. Because the injector is called from inside `client.activate()`, the failure surfaces as a rejected activate for EVERY server-side `withDocument` call (v1 content endpoints, DocumentCopyService, template publish/seed) and for every ops script, not as a startup error. The same unvalidated cast pattern already exists in `AuthService`, so this is a propagation of an existing hazard into a new, broader blast radius rather than a new class of bug; the shipped README template uses a non-empty `10m`, which is why confidence is not high.

samples.summary: Image-upload failures on the new share-link note route are silent: `shareTokenImageUploader` rejects, and the notes engine only console-logs a rejection
samples.evidence: `shareTokenImageUploader` is typed `DocsImageUpload = (file: File) => Promise<string>` (`app/docs/image-insert.ts:15`) and REJECTS on a failed `postShareTokenImage`. The notes engine's contract (`packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:19-26`) is that a host reports its own failure and resolves `null`; a rejection is handled by `failed()`/`startImageUploads` with only `console.error` and a dropped placeholder. The workspace route wraps the uploader and toasts on every failure (`notes-detail.tsx:208-231`), but this new route hands the raw rejecting uploader straight through, so an anonymous editor-role visitor whose upload 4xx/5xxs sees the placeholder vanish with no message and no image.

samples.summary: Flipping the default to enforce converts the documented `attributes: null` fail-closed path from "allowed" to a hard 403 for every caller on a deployment that registered such a method
samples.evidence: `isYorkieAuthEnforced` now returns `true` for an unset variable, and `decide()` returns `{status: 403, allowed: false, reason: 'missing document attributes'}` for any document-scoped method whose `attributes` are absent (`yorkie-auth.controller.ts:228-234`). Yorkie sends `CreateRevision` with `attributes: null` for every caller (documented in `packages/backend/README.md:222-229` and `test/revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:228-241`). Previously a deployment that registered it and configured nothing else landed in shadow mode and the call went through; after this change the same deployment denies `CreateRevision` to everyone including the document owner, so "Name current version" breaks with no config change on the operator's part. The reach is contained because the README explicitly says not to register that method — but the default flip is what removes the safety net that made the mis-registration survivable.

finding.summary: Flipping the enforcement default to "enforce" denies viewer-role share links at attach, because AttachDocument always carries verb `rw`
finding.evidence: `isYorkieAuthEnforced()` returns true for unset, so any deployment that registers the webhook methods and configures nothing else now honors denials. But this repo's own integration test documents the verb behaviour it collides with: packages/backend/test/revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:371-383 — "Deliberately omits `AttachDocument` from the registered set. Empirically … `AttachDocument` always carries verb 'rw' — even for a brand-new local `Document` object with zero local changes … Gating it as the backend README's own walkthrough suggests would deny a viewer's very first attach outright". The documented registration walkthrough (packages/backend/README.md:211, packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:573, docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:201) *does* add `AttachDocument`. In `decide()` → `checkAttribute()` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:257) `verb === 'rw'` ⇒ `needWrite`, and `hasAccess()` line 293 returns `link.role === 'editor'`, so a viewer share link gets 403 on its first attach and the shared document never opens. The same hazard reaches `PushPull`: Yorkie derives the verb from `pack.HasChanges()`, and every mount pushes a change pack containing its `initialPresence` (shared-document.tsx:993 sets presence for the note mount; docs/slides/sheets/board mounts likewise), so a viewer's PushPull can also be classified `rw`. docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:270-283 states this exact risk is *unconfirmed* and that the mitigation is "the rollout must confirm viewer-link attach/PushPull requests actually carry verb `r` (watch the shadow logs) before flipping … =true" — this change removes that staged confirmation by making enforce the default while leaving the verb question open and the README's method list unchanged.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repository. isYorkieAuthEnforced (yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:20-22) returns true when the env var is unset, and the controller wires that straight into the deny path (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:133-135, 168, 185-186). checkAttribute maps verb 'rw' to needWrite (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:257) and hasAccess returns link.role === 'editor' for share visitors (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:293), so a viewer-role attribute with verb 'rw' yields a 403 (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:259-261). The repo's own e2e test documents, from inspecting real webhook bodies, that AttachDocument always carries verb 'rw' even with zero local changes and that gating it "would deny a viewer's very first attach outright" (revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:371-383) — which is why that test deliberately omits AttachDocument from the registered set (revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:384-402). Yet the shipped operator walkthroughs all register AttachDocument (packages/backend/README.md:211, packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:573, docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:201), and self-hosting.md:584-587 tells operators the unset variable means enforce immediately. The design doc still records the verb question as unconfirmed with shadow-mode observation as the required pre-flip step (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:270-283). The viewer path is genuinely reachable: shared-document.tsx:959 injects the share token and the mounts at 975-1021 (incl. 993) pass initialPresence, so the attach/first push carries a change pack. No guard exempts AttachDocument — decide() only short-circuits DetachDocument (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:66,196-198) and client-scoped methods (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:69,220). Result under the documented configuration: a viewer share link 403s on first attach and the shared document never opens — a broken core flow, in the correctness lane. No named refutation ground applies.
